title: Implementation notes — Provider-Neutral Harness Kernel Plan 1
subtitle: Task 8 of 8 · complete · 2026-08-19 20:33
intro: Each item is a decision, deviation, or tradeoff made during implementation. Acknowledge if fine. Discuss to write what should change. Revert to flag for undo.

groups.label: Task 8 — Coverage gate and pipeline wiring

items.title: Adapted grant tests to the Docker sandbox API

body.Spec said: Load grant.ts through the superseded lockedCoreModule and lockedRealm helpers.
body.What I did: Used sandboxCall and the worker-local SHA-256 port from the implemented Task 3 harness.
body.Why: The committed harness is Docker-contained and has no locked-realm.ts compatibility layer.
body.Risk: The public Task 4 core interfaces are unchanged; only the test transport differs.

items.title: Made coverage aggregation incremental under the fixed memory ceiling

body.Spec said: Run every fresh-worker core test under c8 --all --100 inside a 256 MB container.
body.What I did: Enabled c8's built-in --merge-async mode, then closed the four legitimate grant coverage gaps. The combined gate now passes at 100%.
body.Why: Task 4 adds many fresh workers, each producing raw V8 coverage; the current single aggregation process no longer fits the accepted memory limit.
body.Risk: The sandbox remains fixed at 256 MB and every core call still uses a fresh worker; only c8's raw-report merge strategy changed.

body.What I did: Implemented capability-grant validation and verified the complete PNH and X1 suites.
body.Followup: PNH: 21 tests with 100% statements, branches, functions, and lines. X1: 169 tests passed.

body.Spec said: Return a Promise from consume and reject ambiguous storage failures.
body.What I did: Declared MemoryReplayLedger.consume async so an injected storage failure becomes a rejected Promise.
body.Why: Calling the failure hook before constructing a Promise threw synchronously and broke the port's asynchronous contract.
body.Risk: None for callers using await. The change makes failure behavior match ReplayLedger.consume.

items.title: Tested the runtime protocol through the sandbox

body.What I did: Kept the canonical decision constant in core and exposed a pure consumeDecisions function so the test can read it through sandboxCall.
body.Why: The first implementation imported the constant directly. The authoritative harness rejected that runtime core import, as designed.
body.Risk: The core gains one read-only helper. Tests retain the rule that every runtime core access runs in a fresh worker.

body.What I did: Implemented the at-most-once consume port, in-memory reference adapter, and T22 conformance coverage.
body.Followup: PNH: 27 tests with 100% statements, branches, functions, and lines. X1: 169 tests passed.

items.title: Moved raw coverage reports to an ephemeral volume

body.What I did: Mounted an anonymous Docker volume at /coverage and kept reports under /coverage/raw.
body.Why: All 35 tests and 100% coverage completed, but accumulated V8 reports filled the 256 MB /tmp filesystem before c8 could write its summary.
body.Risk: The volume is temporary and has no host-path binding. The container remains read-only, networkless, and capped at 256 MB of memory.

body.What I did: Implemented the tamper-evident evidence hash chain with checkpoint, sequence, link, digest, and injected-hash validation.
body.Followup: PNH: 35 tests with 100% statements, branches, functions, and lines. X1: 169 tests passed.

items.title: Non-finite telemetry fails at the JSON boundary

body.Spec said: Reject non-finite duration values in broker receipt validation.
body.What I did: Asserted that the sandbox rejects NaN before core execution and separately covered negative, fractional, string, missing, and null telemetry inside core.
body.Why: The JSON-only worker boundary cannot serialize non-finite numbers. Core retains its Number.isFinite check for direct typed callers.
body.Risk: None at the sandbox boundary; malformed non-finite values fail earlier than the receipt reject-code layer.

body.What I did: Implemented exact broker receipt validation for identity, digests, telemetry, schema shape, and normalized-copy isolation.
body.Followup: PNH: 46 tests with 100% statements, branches, functions, and lines. X1: 169 tests passed.

body.Spec said: Wire npm run test:pnh to the authoritative Docker-contained test and coverage gate.
body.What I did: Confirmed the existing test:pnh script already invokes node pnh/harness/run-sandbox.mjs, so no package.json change was needed.
body.Why: Tasks 3 and 4 established the final sandbox runner before Task 8.
body.Risk: None. CI calls the same command verified locally.

items.title: Proved the coverage gate fails closed

body.What I did: Temporarily added one uncovered branch and one unimported TypeScript source file. The authoritative command failed on both, then returned to 100% after the probes were removed.
body.Why: A passing baseline alone would not prove that --all includes untouched source files or that branch coverage is enforced.
body.Risk: None. Both probes were removed before the final verification run.

body.What I did: Added the PNH contributor guide and the isolated push and pull-request CI workflow, then verified its YAML structure and command wiring.
body.Followup: PNH: 46 tests with 100% statements, branches, functions, and lines. X1: 169 tests passed. All 8 kernel-plan tasks are complete.
